seoTitle: How to Add a Watermark on Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: Add a text or image watermark in Google Docs from Insert > Page elements > Watermark, why it won't show up in pageless documents, and how to edit or remove it later.
intro:
Google Docs has a built-in watermark tool tucked a couple of menus deep. Once you find it, stamping a repeating "Confidential" label or a company logo across every page takes under a minute. It moved recently, which is why some older tutorials point to the wrong menu, and it silently doesn't work at all on one common document format.

A light "Draft" or "Confidential" watermark suits a document still under review; a logo suits a polished report going to a client. Either way, keep it faint enough that it sits behind your text rather than competing with it.
prerequisites: The document must be in pages format. Google Docs doesn't offer the watermark tool in pageless documents, and switching an already-watermarked document to pageless hides the watermark without deleting it.

steps.heading: Open Insert, then Page elements, then Watermark
steps.body:
First, check the document isn't in pageless format; if it is, the Watermark option won't do anything useful. From the top menu, click Insert, then hover Page elements, a submenu that opens with Table of contents, Header, Footer, Watermark, Page numbers, and Footnote. Watermark used to sit as its own top-level item directly under Insert, so if you've used this before and can't find it, that's the change: it's now nested inside Page elements.

Clicking Watermark opens a panel on the right with Image and Text tabs at the top, where the rest of the setup happens.

image.caption: The Insert menu with Page elements expanded, revealing Watermark alongside Header, Footer, and Page numbers, plus the Watermark panel that opens on the right.

steps.heading: Type your text watermark
steps.body:
With the Text tab selected, type your watermark into the field, something like "Draft," "Confidential," or a company name. Google Docs renders it as large, light, repeating text diagonally across the page behind your content, updating live as you type. Keep it to a short phrase; a full sentence stops reading as a watermark and starts reading as a diagonal paragraph.

The watermark applies to the whole document at once. There's no separate step to copy it onto each page.

image.caption: A text watermark applied to the document, showing as large, light, diagonal text running behind the body content on every page.

steps.heading: Adjust the font, transparency, and orientation
steps.body: Below the text field, the formatting section changes the font (a bolder face like Impact reads more clearly than the default at a glance), plus bold, italic, underline, and color. The transparency slider is the setting most worth tuning: too opaque and it competes with your real text, too faint and it's pointless. Something in the 50 to 70% range works for most fonts. Below that, a toggle switches the orientation between Diagonal and Horizontal.

image.caption: The Watermark panel's formatting controls: font, transparency slider, and a toggle between diagonal and horizontal orientation.

steps.heading: Use an image watermark instead of text
steps.body:
To stamp a logo instead of a line of text, click the Image tab at the top of the same panel. That switches it to an upload control pulling from your computer, Google Drive, a URL, or your camera; the same transparency and placement controls apply once the image is in.

If the image watermark shows odd gaps or a visible box around parts of it, a text background color elsewhere on the page is sitting on top of the watermark rather than behind it. Removing that background color usually clears it up.

steps.heading: Edit or remove the watermark later
steps.body:
The fastest way to edit an existing watermark is to right-click it directly on the page, choose Select watermark, then click Edit watermark below it. Reopening Insert → Page elements → Watermark brings up the same panel too, and it's the only route to actually delete one: click Remove watermark at the bottom.

Swapping one watermark for another works the same way as editing: open the panel, retype the text or switch tabs to move from text to image, and the change applies instantly across every page.

troubleshooting.problem: Watermark does nothing, or the option seems missing
troubleshooting.cause: The document is in pageless format. Google Docs doesn't support watermarks there.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch the document to pages format, then insert the watermark.

troubleshooting.cause: The document was switched to pageless format at some point, which hides watermarks without deleting them.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch back to pages format and the watermark reappears.

troubleshooting.problem: An image watermark has visible gaps or boxy edges
troubleshooting.cause: Text elsewhere on the page has a background color sitting on top of the watermark instead of behind it.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the background color from that text.

faq.question: Can I use my own logo as a watermark in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. Open Insert → Page elements → Watermark, switch to the Image tab, and upload a logo from your computer, Google Drive, a URL, or your camera.

faq.question: Why doesn't the Watermark tool do anything in my document?
faq.answer: Check whether the document is in pageless format. Google Docs doesn't support watermarks there; switch to pages format first.

faq.question: Does the watermark appear on every page automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. Once applied, it repeats across every page automatically, with no need to reinsert it page by page.

faq.question: How do I remove a watermark once it's added?
faq.answer: Reopen Insert → Page elements → Watermark and click Remove watermark at the bottom of the panel.

faq.question: Is there a faster way to edit an existing watermark than reopening the menu?
faq.answer: Right-click the watermark on the page, choose Select watermark, then click Edit watermark. That opens the same panel without going back through Insert.

faq.question: I can't find Watermark under Insert anymore. Where did it go?
faq.answer: Google moved it into a submenu: click Insert, then hover Page elements, and Watermark is listed there alongside Header, Footer, and Page numbers.

references.label: Insert, edit, or delete watermarks (official Google Docs Editors Help)

verifiedNote: Click path and screenshots come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025/2026. Menu location, the remove-watermark step, and the formatting options were re-checked against Google's official Docs Editors Help in September 2026. That check added two things the article was missing entirely: watermarks don't work in pageless-format documents, and an existing watermark can be edited faster with a right-click rather than reopening the Insert menu. An unverifiable claim about a 100-character limit on the watermark text was removed, since it isn't stated in Google's documentation and couldn't be confirmed.
